chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:
I asked him about the speech that is recited between the two takbirs in the two Eid prayers, and he said: 'Whatever good speech you wish.'

key_terms.التَّكْبِيرَتَيْنِ: The two takbirs (specifically the first and sixth in Eid prayers)
key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: The two Eid festivals (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha)

ai.seo_question: What should be recited between the takbirs in Eid prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS), the flexibility in reciting between the first and sixth takbirs during Eid prayers is highlighted, allowing for any 'good speech' (kalasan). This reflects the Shia scholarly view that while specific dhikr is recommended, the absence of a rigidly prescribed text emphasizes the spirit of gratitude and praise over formalistic constraint. The hadith underscores the principle of ease in worship, aligning with the broader Islamic legal maxim of permissibility unless evidence dictates otherwise.
